problem: The line differ kept a full copy of its working array for every edit step. Diffing two large, very different files (60k lines each) would try to allocate ~19 GB and take down the server for every agent.
fix: Store only the diagonals each step needs (O(D²) instead of O(D·(N+M))) under a fixed 80 MB budget, falling back to replace-all beyond it. Diff of 2×60k lines now takes 0.16 s.

problem: Racily-clean files: a same-size edit made within the filesystem's timestamp granularity after checkout looked unchanged, so `graft commit` silently dropped it.
fix: Index entries record when they were written; files modified that close to the record time are hashed instead of trusted by stat.

problem: In a sparse workspace, creating a file outside the sparse paths that already existed upstream would overwrite the upstream file without anyone having seen it.
fix: `graft commit` checks the server for such paths and refuses with a hint to `graft add-sparse` first (`--force` to override).

problem: Bodies that were JSON but not objects (null, arrays), non-string fields, control characters in paths and malformed URL encoding crashed handlers with 500 errors.
fix: Validate body shape and field types at the edge; reject control characters in paths; return 400 with a precise message.

problem: When landing on a branch other than main, the commit's base still defaulted to main, so edits were resolved against the wrong file versions (or failed with 'file does not exist').
fix: Base defaults to the branch being landed on.

problem: Repository creation wrote the repo row, root changeset and main ref in separate transactions; a crash between them left a repo with no main branch.
fix: Nested-transaction support; repo, root and ref are created atomically.

problem: A move could reuse a source path that another entry in the same commit also changed, producing a changeset that depended on entry order.
fix: A path may be claimed once per commit; moves onto themselves are rejected.

problem: When a commit turned out to be already on main (a no-op land), the workspace kept its old base, so the next sync re-merged changes it already had.
fix: Every land outcome moves the workspace to the branch head.

problem: The diff renderer skipped any line starting with '---' or '+++', so removed or added lines like '-- SQL comment' or '++i' vanished from the changeset view.
fix: Only the file header before the first hunk is skipped.

problem: `graft diff` printed raw bytes for binary files.
fix: Binary files print a one-line notice.

problem: Blame loaded every changeset's change list while walking history, so its cost grew with the whole repository's history.
fix: Walk only the changesets that touched the path (via the path index).

problem: A regex search could pin the single server thread on pathological patterns over minified lines.
fix: Cap query length and skip very long lines in regex mode.

problem: The Docker image and launcher always passed --experimental-sqlite, which only some Node versions need; a stray GRAFT_WEB_ROOT="" served index.html from the current directory.
fix: The launcher detects whether node:sqlite needs the flag; empty web roots are ignored; a read-token-only config now warns that writes are disabled.

problem: After an idle period, a pooled keep-alive socket the server had closed made the next request fail with ECONNRESET.
fix: Server keep-alive raised to 65 s; the client retries once on a stale socket.

problem: Every CLI commit did 3+ round trips plus a full workspace scan and manifest download after landing.
fix: Small changes go inline with the commit; fast-forwards fetch nothing; rebases fetch only the paths that changed.

problem: graft_commit labeled added files as modified.
fix: The commit response now reports added/modified/deleted per file.
